countries.name: Canada
countries.admission: Apply directly to a recognised institution and confirm programme-specific academic and language requirements. For post-secondary study, check that the institution is a Designated Learning Institution (DLI).
visa_steps: Obtain a letter of acceptance from a DLI.
Check whether a provincial or territorial attestation letter (PAL/TAL) is required; exemptions apply.
Prepare proof of funds, identity documents and any requested medical or police documents.
Apply online and follow biometrics or additional-document instructions.
If approved, review the letter of introduction and any travel document requirements before departure.
documents: Letter of acceptance from a DLI
PAL/TAL where required
Proof of funds for tuition, living costs and travel
Valid passport and identity documents
Medical exam or police certificate if requested
countries.funds: The required amount depends on tuition, family size and where you will study. Check IRCC's current proof-of-funds table before applying.
countries.work: Work eligibility and hour limits depend on the conditions of the study permit and current IRCC rules. Check the official work-while-studying page; do not assume every student may work.
countries.poststudy: A Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) may be available only if the student, institution and programme meet the rules in force when applying.
countries.costs: Tuition and living costs vary by institution, province, city and programme. Use institution fee schedules and current government guidance.
countries.notes: Quebec has additional provincial requirements. PAL/TAL exemptions and PGWP rules can change; verify them for the exact programme and application date.

countries.name: United States
countries.admission: Apply to a Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP)-certified school. The institution sets academic, English-language, testing and financial admission requirements.
visa_steps: Apply to an SEVP-certified school and receive an acceptance.
Pay the I-901 SEVIS fee when required and obtain Form I-20 from the school.
Complete the DS-160 visa application and pay the visa application fee.
Schedule and attend the visa interview with the required documents.
Follow the visa and entry instructions; a visa does not guarantee admission at the border.
documents: Form I-20 issued by the school
Valid passport
DS-160 confirmation and visa appointment documents
Evidence of funds for tuition and living costs
Academic records and any additional interview evidence
countries.funds: Applicants must demonstrate credible funding for the costs of study and living. The school documents estimated costs on the I-20; check its instructions and consular requirements.
countries.work: F-1 employment is restricted. On-campus work and authorised training options have specific conditions; obtain the required authorisation before working.
countries.poststudy: Optional Practical Training (OPT), including STEM OPT extensions for eligible students, is subject to detailed eligibility and authorisation rules.
countries.costs: Tuition and living expenses vary widely by institution and location. Compare the institution's published cost of attendance and financial aid.
countries.notes: Visa issuance, interview availability and entry decisions are individual. Do not begin employment without the required authorisation.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.admission: Apply to a licensed student sponsor. You generally need an unconditional offer and a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS). Academic and English-language requirements are set by the provider.
visa_steps: Receive an offer from a licensed student sponsor.
Obtain your CAS and check course and sponsor details.
Prepare evidence of funds and English ability where required.
Apply online for the Student visa, pay the fee and Immigration Health Surcharge if applicable.
Complete identity verification or attend a biometrics appointment as instructed.
documents: CAS reference number
Valid passport
Proof of funds if required
English-language evidence if required
ATAS certificate or parental consent where applicable
countries.funds: The financial requirement depends on course fees, study location and maintenance rules. Check the current GOV.UK amount and required holding period before applying.
countries.work: Work permission depends on course level, sponsor and visa conditions. Check the conditions on the eVisa and current GOV.UK rules.
countries.poststudy: The Graduate visa is subject to eligibility and the rules in force when applying. Check current duration, application timing and qualifying course requirements.
countries.costs: Tuition varies by university and course. Living-cost requirements differ between London and outside London; consult current official guidance.
countries.notes: Dependants are restricted for many taught courses. ATAS applies to certain sensitive subject areas and nationalities.

countries.name: France
countries.permit_name: Long-stay student visa (VLS-TS) or other student residence route
countries.admission: Requirements depend on the institution, programme and applicant's country of residence. Campus France procedures apply in designated countries; check the relevant country-specific process.
visa_steps: Choose a recognised programme and obtain admission or pre-enrolment evidence.
Check whether the Etudes en France procedure applies in your country.
Use France-Visas to identify the correct visa and document checklist.
Submit the application through the designated process and attend an appointment if required.
After arrival, validate a VLS-TS online within the required period, if that is the visa issued.
documents: Admission or pre-enrolment evidence
Passport and visa application forms
Proof of resources meeting the current threshold
Proof of accommodation where requested
Health insurance and civil-status documents where required
countries.funds: Applicants must show sufficient resources under the current French rules. Confirm the amount and acceptable evidence on France-Visas and Campus France.
countries.work: Student work is generally subject to an annual legal limit. Confirm the current limit and any exceptions before accepting work.
countries.poststudy: A temporary residence route to seek employment or create a business may be available to eligible graduates; conditions depend on qualification and circumstances.
countries.costs: Tuition differs between public institutions, private schools and programmes. Check the institution's current fee schedule and any differentiated fees or exemptions.
countries.notes: The visa route and Campus France process depend on nationality and country of residence. VLS-TS validation is time-sensitive.

countries.name: Germany
countries.permit_name: National visa for study, followed by residence permit where required
countries.admission: Check whether your school-leaving certificate or previous degree qualifies for the chosen programme. Some applicants need Studienkolleg or a recognised assessment; language requirements are programme-specific.
visa_steps: Check admission eligibility and apply to the university or preparatory course.
Confirm whether you need a student visa before travel.
Arrange accepted proof of financing, such as a blocked account, scholarship or formal commitment where permitted.
Apply through the responsible German mission and provide the required documents.
After arrival, complete local registration and apply for a residence permit if required.
documents: Admission letter or evidence of applicant status where applicable
Proof of financing using an accepted method
Valid passport
Health insurance evidence
Academic qualifications and language evidence
countries.funds: The blocked-account amount and accepted alternatives can change. Use the current German mission and official study portal guidance; do not rely on older annual figures.
countries.work: Student work rights are governed by current residence law and may differ by permit status. Check the current official guidance before working.
countries.poststudy: Eligible graduates of German higher education institutions may apply for a residence permit to seek qualified employment, subject to current conditions.
countries.costs: Many public universities charge no general tuition but semester contributions apply; exceptions and tuition-charging states or programmes exist. Verify institution-specific fees.
countries.notes: Admission recognition and visa requirements depend on nationality and prior education. A blocked account is not the only possible financing route.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.permit_name: Residence permit for study; entry MVV may also be required
countries.admission: Apply to a recognised Dutch higher education institution. The institution sets academic and language requirements and generally acts as the immigration sponsor.
visa_steps: Apply to a recognised institution and meet its admission conditions.
The institution submits the residence-permit application and MVV application if needed.
Provide proof of sufficient funds and other requested documents.
Complete any required civic integration or biometrics steps as instructed.
After arrival, collect the residence document and comply with study-progress requirements.
documents: Admission/enrolment evidence
Valid passport
Proof of sufficient funds
Proof of payment or financial arrangements as required
TB test or other health documentation if applicable
countries.funds: The required monthly study norm is updated periodically. Check the IND study permit page for the current amount and whether tuition must be demonstrated separately.
countries.work: Paid employment usually requires a work permit arranged by the employer, with limited exceptions such as permitted seasonal or self-employed work. Check current IND rules.
countries.poststudy: Eligible graduates may apply for the one-year orientation-year residence permit, subject to qualification and timing rules.
countries.costs: Tuition differs between EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA students and between institutions. Housing availability and costs vary substantially by city.
countries.notes: Only recognised sponsors can apply for the student residence permit. Students must meet study-progress requirements.

countries.name: Australia
countries.admission: Apply to a provider and course registered for overseas students (CRICOS). Providers set academic, English-language and other admission requirements.
visa_steps: Choose a CRICOS-registered course and receive a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE).
Arrange Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the required period.
Prepare evidence for the Genuine Student requirement and financial capacity.
Submit the Student visa (subclass 500) application online with supporting documents.
Complete health, biometrics or character checks if requested.
documents: Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
OSHC evidence
Evidence addressing the Genuine Student requirement
Financial capacity evidence
English, health and character documents as requested
countries.funds: Financial capacity thresholds and accepted evidence can change. Check the current Department of Home Affairs checklist for the applicant's circumstances.
countries.work: Work limits apply during study periods, with different rules during scheduled course breaks and for certain research students. Check current visa conditions.
countries.poststudy: The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) has distinct streams, qualification and age requirements. Check current rules before planning around it.
countries.costs: Tuition depends on provider, course and study level. Living costs vary by city; use official planning resources and provider estimates.
countries.notes: The Genuine Student assessment and evidence requirements are central to the application. A CoE alone does not guarantee a visa.

countries.name: China
countries.permit_name: X1 visa for long-term study or X2 visa for short-term study
countries.admission: Apply to a university authorised to enrol international students. Programme, language, medical and academic requirements vary by institution and scholarship route.
visa_steps: Obtain admission from the host university and the official study-visa documents it issues (commonly JW201/JW202 or the relevant confirmation).
Check the responsible Chinese embassy or visa application service for the current X1/X2 category and checklist.
Submit the visa application and attend any required appointment.
For X1 long-term study, follow the local entry-exit administration instructions to apply for a residence permit after arrival within the required period.
Keep the university informed and comply with local residence registration requirements.
documents: University admission notice
Official study-visa supporting form/document issued for the programme
Valid passport and visa application form
Medical examination or other supporting documents if requested
Proof of funding and accommodation if requested
countries.funds: Funding evidence and document requirements depend on the visa office, university and scholarship route. Follow the current embassy/visa-centre checklist.
countries.work: Do not assume student work is permitted. Off-campus work or internships require compliance with immigration and university approval rules; verify before starting.
countries.poststudy: Post-study residence and employment are not automatic. Graduates must qualify under a separate immigration or employment route.
countries.costs: Tuition, accommodation and living costs vary by city, university and programme. Confirm the current fee schedule directly with the university.
countries.notes: Visa forms, procedures and service providers vary by country of application. Check the local Chinese embassy or official visa application centre and the university's international office.
